# David Packer Recommends Increasing Sets Then Decreasing Rest To Progress Front Lever Pull-Up Reps

David Packer recommends increasing the number of sets of one rep before moving to sets of two reps, then decreasing rest periods to progress front lever pull-up repetitions. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]

## Details

- First, increase sets of one rep, for example from five sets of one rep up to 10 with a one and a half minute rest, then up to 15 sets of one rep, progressing week to week. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- Then decrease the rest period from a minute and a half to a minute, then to 45 seconds, then 30 seconds. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- After that, you will have two sets of two reps, then half three reps and one rep, then it will all become two reps. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- He reckons 12 to 15 sets of one with one and a half minute rest was when he could do one set of two or consecutive sets of two. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]
- It is not about doing everything sets of two or everything sets of one, you just need to do more work than last week or last session, tiny increments. [src: vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ]

## Evidence

- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "first thing i would do would um i would be doing i would increase my sets so i'll do you know sets of one rep say if i'm doing five sets of one rep um you know get to 10 with a one and a half minute rest"
- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "maybe i'll go up to 15 sets of one right this is progressing week to week and then i would decrease my rest period down to cut it off by 30 seconds or you know from a minute and a half to a minute"
- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "or even like you know 45 seconds 30 seconds yeah and then i'll you know before i know it i'll have um two sets of two reps and then i'll do half three reps and one rep and then it'll all become two reps at one level"
- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "i reckon 15 12 to 15 sets of one with one one and a half minute rest was when i could yeah one just one set of two or consecutive sets of two"
- vid-lkcLJc2c0NQ (David Packer): "the thing is that it's not really about like i want to do everything sets of two or everything sets of one i just need to do more work than i did last week or you know last session"
